metadata.title: LIAQAT ALI vs JUDGE, FAMILY COURT, HAFIZABAD and 3 others

full_text:
2010 Y L R 1136

[Lahore]

Before Muhammad Ashraf Bhatti, J

LIAQAT ALI---Petitioner

Versus

JUDGE, FAMILY COURT, HAFIZABAD and 3
others---Respondents

Writ Petition No.7654 of 2009, decided on 2nd July,
2009.

West Pakistan Family Courts Act (XXXV of 1964)---

----S. 5 Sched. & S.17A---Constitution of
Pakistan (1973), Art.199---Constitutional petition---Suit for
maintenance---Maintenance allowance to two minors was awarded respectively at
the rate of Rs.1200 and Rs.1000 with 20% annual increase, but
defendant/judgment-debtor had failed to pay the same and the defence of
defendant was struck off---Maintenance allowance granted to the mother of the
minors was decreed ex parte, which could be challenged by the defendant before
the appropriate forum---Counsel for the defendant had opted not to press
constitutional petition to seek remedy before
the court of competent jurisdiction--Constitutional
petition was dismissed as having not been pressed.

Shahid Ali Shakir for Petitioner.

Muhammad Shahid Usman for Respondents Nos.2 to 4.

ORDER

MUHAMMAD ASHRAF BHATTI, J.---This is a
petition filed by Liaqat Ali to challenge the vires of the order dated
20-12-2008 whereby the maintenance allowance at the rate of Rs.1,200 and
Rs.1,000 with 20% annual increase was awarded to the minors children of the
petitioner but failed to pay the same. The learned Trial Court struck off the
defence of the petitioner on 28-10-2008. The application moved there against
also met with the same fate.

2. As regards the maintenance allowance granted to
the mother of the minors, namely, Kausar Parveen respondent No.2 learned
counsel for the respondent states at bar that the case was fixed for ex parte
evidence on 21-1-2009 and was subsequently decreed in her favour which can be
challenged by the petitioner before the appropriate forum.

3. When confronted with the above position of the
case, learned counsel for the petitioner has opted not to press this petition
to seek remedy before the Court of competent jurisdiction. Accordingly this
writ petition is dismissed as having not been pressed.

H.B.T./L-6/L Petition
dismissed.
